headline.caveat: ~$10B program for up to 1GW of AMD MI-series AI infrastructure in Saudi Arabia (announced May 2025, scaled through 2026); program-level figure — formal contract values undisclosed.

realized_to_date.caveat: Initial tranches (first ~100s of MW) deploying 2026; paid amounts undisclosed — Humain discloses GPU counts and MW, not dollars.

nature_md: Humain — Saudi Arabia's PIF-owned AI company — is deploying up to 1GW of AMD Instinct MI-series compute in its Saudi AI factories under a ~$10B multi-year collaboration announced May 2025 (alongside its larger Nvidia program; Humain deliberately dual-sources silicon). AMD also took a small equity/partnership interest in the program structure at announcement. Part of Humain's 6.6GW-by-2034 pipeline serving sovereign AI and export inference capacity; US export-license conditions apply to all shipments.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: Humain (state-owned, no public accounts) capitalizes the systems as data-center assets funded by PIF equity; commitments are program announcements rather than audited obligations — dollar realization depends on export licenses and buildout pace.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: AMD books data-center GPU/systems revenue on delivery; the Humain program is one of the two GW-scale anchor deployments (with OpenAI's 6GW) validating its rack-scale roadmap. Contract-level splits undisclosed.

both_sides_md: **Bull:** sovereign capital is the marginal buyer that diversifies AMD away from hyperscaler dependence, at GW scale. **Bear:** headline sovereign programs habitually outrun realized deployment (see 9.2b data gaps — Humain contract dollars are undisclosed); export-control policy can re-scope the deal at any time.
